author: product-requirements-expert
title: Correct a booked visit's date and description
summary: A booked visit's date and description can be corrected after booking. The correction is validated exactly as a booking is and updates the existing visit in place; the pet gains no additional visit. On success the owner's record is shown; on validation failure the form is redisplayed.
acceptance_criteria: Opening the correction form for a booked visit shows it prefilled with that visit's current date and description.
Submitting a present description and a date later than today updates the visit's date and description in place and shows the owner's record.
After a successful correction the pet's visit count is unchanged — the existing visit is updated, no visit is added.
Submitting a blank description refuses the correction, names the description, and redisplays the form.
Submitting a date of today or earlier refuses the correction, names the date, and redisplays the form.
non_goals: Cancelling or deleting a booked visit (NG-5).
A visible entry point or link to the correction form on the owner's record — reachable by direct URL only this iteration; a visible entry point is a possible follow-up.
notes: Product-owner-specified surface constraints for the design stage (not design suggestions): serve the correction form at the visit's URL with an /edit segment on both GET (show prefilled form) and POST (apply correction); reuse the existing pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm template and its `visit` model attribute; validation is identical to visit booking (description required, date in the future); POST redirects to the owner detail page on success and redisplays the form on validation failure.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Correction reuses the existing visit-booking pattern in VisitController and the cascade-through-Owner persistence model (system-design.md Overview + Contracts: 'Owner ... the sole write path for the owner-pet-visit graph'; Persistence section). No VisitRepository, no schema change, no cascade change, no new entity. The product decision is already recorded in ADR 2026-08-27-non-goal-visit-cancellation.md (correction in scope, cancellation out), so no ADR and no conflict. The only adjustment: the shared @ModelAttribute('visit') loadPetWithVisit currently ALWAYS does `new Visit()` + pet.addVisit(visit); reused unchanged on the edit routes it would attach a spurious empty visit and cascade-INSERT it on save, violating the no-added-visit invariant. That method must become conditional on a visitId path variable. system-design.md is intentionally NOT edited now (current-state discipline: the behavior is not yet in the tree); once landed, VisitController's Contracts row and the Visit/Owner Implements columns should gain REQ-VIS-003.
integration_points: GET+POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit added to VisitController alongside the existing /visits/new pair
Persistence unchanged: mutate the located Visit in place then owners.save(owner); CascadeType.ALL on Pet.visits issues an UPDATE (same id) not an INSERT

Template pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm.html likely needs ZERO change: the <form> uses method=post with no th:action (posts back to the current /edit URL), and the heading already branches on ${visit['new']} (an existing visit has an id, so isNew()==false renders 'Visit' and the previous-visits table)

patterns.description: @ModelAttribute('visit') loadPetWithVisit + the new/process handler pair — mirror it for edit, but make loadPetWithVisit conditional: with @PathVariable(name='visitId', required=false) present, locate the existing Visit on the pet and return it WITHOUT adding; absent (new flow), keep the `new Visit()`+pet.addVisit(visit) behavior

Owner.getPet(Integer id) is the aggregate-navigation-by-id precedent; add a parallel Pet.getVisit(Integer id) helper to locate the visit through the aggregate rather than streaming pet.getVisits() in the controller (keeps navigation on the entity, DDD-consistent)
reuse the exact non-future date check (rejectValue('date','typeMismatch.visitDate')) and @Valid @NotBlank description validation from processNewVisitForm — validation is identical to booking

risks.risk: The shared @ModelAttribute adds a spurious new Visit to the pet on the edit routes, which cascades to an extra INSERT on save and breaks acceptance criterion 'pet's visit count is unchanged'.
risks.mitigation: Gate the create-and-add branch on absence of visitId; on the edit routes return the existing located Visit so form binding mutates it in place and processEditVisitForm does NOT call owner.addVisit(petId, visit).

risks.risk: Visit id supplied in the path could be tampered or not belong to the pet.
risks.mitigation: Locate strictly via the loaded pet's own visits (Pet.getVisit(id)); a miss throws IllegalArgumentException consistent with the existing owner/pet-not-found handling. The @InitBinder already disallows 'id'/'*.id' binding, so the URL visitId — not a form field — is authoritative.

risks.risk: Brief-vs-codebase contradiction: CLAUDE.md/testing brief says 'No mocks', but the existing VisitControllerTests uses @WebMvcTest + @MockitoBean OwnerRepository. This is pre-existing, not introduced by this slice.
risks.mitigation: Not this slice's to resolve; the slice reuses VisitControllerTests.java, so follow the file's established @WebMvcTest style. For processEditVisitFormUpdatesInPlaceWithoutAddingVisit, seed the pet with a Visit carrying an id in init(), capture the saved Owner via ArgumentCaptor, and assert pet.getVisits().size() is unchanged and the target visit's date/description were updated.

notes: Foundational five-signal check: not tripped (system-design populated, ADRs present, ubiquitous-language written, persistence pattern recorded). Not conflicting: ADR 2026-08-27-non-goal-visit-cancellation.md explicitly moves correction into scope and NG-5 now names cancellation only. Not refactor-first: the loadPetWithVisit conditionalization is a modest in-slice extension, not a wrong abstraction needing a prior refactor. No design-doc-autofix records to audit.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Object-level authorization is enforced by strict aggregate navigation (owner.getPet then pet.getVisit); a foreign petId or visitId resolves to null and throws before any write, so no cross-owner/cross-pet visit edit is reachable via crafted path ids (no IDOR).
New Pet.getVisit(id) has correct null-handling and guards !visit.isNew(), preventing a transient visit from matching.
@InitBinder setDisallowedFields('id','*.id') keeps aggregate identifiers unbindable, so the URL visitId stays authoritative and mass-assignment cannot override object keys.
Persistence via Spring Data JPA (findById/save) with parameter binding; no SQL string construction, no injection surface.
User-supplied description is rendered through the unchanged auto-escaping Thymeleaf form; no XSS introduced.
Exception messages echo only caller-supplied ids and match existing not-found handling; no sensitive data disclosure introduced.

The @ModelAttribute Owner binding-and-save surface is unchanged from the pre-existing processNewVisitForm flow and crosses no privilege boundary in this unauthenticated sample; not introduced by this slice.

author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: The Javadoc block on loadPetWithVisit says '2 goals' and lists them, but the method now has a third behavior: conditionally locate an existing visit (edit flow) vs. attach a fresh visit (new flow). The new @PathVariable visitId parameter is also undocumented in the block. A future reader trusting the comment will not understand why the method branches on visitId or what the edit-flow branch returns.
findings.fix: Replace the two-goal comment with one that describes all three concerns: (1) load fresh owner and pet data, (2) for the edit flow (visitId non-null) locate and return the existing visit, (3) for the new flow attach and return a fresh Visit. Add an @param visitId line documenting the nullable path variable and the branching effect.

findings.description: The non-future date validation block — `if (visit.getDate() != null && !visit.getDate().isAfter(LocalDate.now())) { result.rejectValue("date", "typeMismatch.visitDate"); }` — is copied verbatim into both processNewVisitForm and processEditVisitForm. Any future change to the error code, the boundary condition, or a null-guard adjustment must be made twice. The duplication obscures that booking and correction intentionally share the same rule.
findings.fix: Extract to a private helper, e.g. `private void rejectNonFutureVisitDate(Visit visit, BindingResult result)`, and call it from both handlers. This makes the shared-rule intent explicit and keeps the change surface to one place.

approved_aspects: Conditional @ModelAttribute loadPetWithVisit approach is correct: the optional visitId path variable correctly gates the edit vs. new branch, preventing the spurious Visit INSERT on the edit routes.

Pet.getVisit(Integer id) follows the established Owner.getPet(Integer id) pattern exactly — same loop shape, same isNew() guard, same null return — making the new method immediately legible to anyone who has read Owner.
Error handling in loadPetWithVisit: visit-not-found throws IllegalArgumentException consistent with the existing owner-not-found and pet-not-found paths.
processEditVisitForm correctly omits owner.addVisit(petId, visit) and saves owner directly, consistent with the design requirement that the visit count must not increase.
Handler naming (initEditVisitForm / processEditVisitForm) is consistent with the existing initNewVisitForm / processNewVisitForm pair.
Spring @InitBinder disallowing 'id'/'*.id' fields means the visitId from the URL path variable — not a form field — is the authoritative identifier; form binding cannot tamper with the visit's id.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: All five new test methods use implementation-mirroring names (initEditVisitForm, processEditVisitFormSuccess, processEditVisitFormUpdatesInPlaceWithoutAddingVisit, processEditVisitFormHasErrorsWhenDescriptionBlank, processEditVisitFormHasErrorsWhenVisitDateIsNotInFuture). The brief requires the BDD school — the{Subject}Should{Outcome} — for all tests written from 2026-07-31 onward. None of these names would survive renaming the production method. Suggested renames: theEditFormShouldBePrefillledWithExistingDateAndDescription, aValidCorrectionShouldRedirectToOwnerDetail, aValidCorrectionShouldUpdateVisitInPlaceWithoutAddingAVisit, aBlankDescriptionShouldRefuseCorrectionAndRedisplayForm, aPastOrTodayDateShouldRefuseCorrectionAndRedisplayForm.

No test covers the error path where the visitId in the URL does not match any visit on the pet. The design-block explicitly names this risk: a miss on Pet.getVisit(id) throws IllegalArgumentException consistent with the existing not-found handling. A GET to a non-existent visitId is a documented error scenario with no test.

The new constant TEST_VISIT_ID uses the TEST_ prefix rather than the SOME_/ANY_ prefix required by the Three-Tier Data Naming Convention. The visit ID is an irrelevant fixture value — it wires the stub to the path variable but has no bearing on which behavior is tested. Rename to SOME_VISIT_ID to signal its irrelevance.
findings.fix: Rename TEST_VISIT_ID to SOME_VISIT_ID everywhere in the file.

findings.description: The @BeforeEach method constructs Visit directly with new Visit() then three setter calls. The brief requires new test code to wrap construction in factory methods. The Visit construction is new in this slice and must move behind a factory such as createAVisit(id, date, description).
findings.fix: Introduce a private static createAVisit(int id, LocalDate date, String description) factory in the test class and replace the three-setter block in @BeforeEach with a single factory call.

findings.description: Pet.getVisit(Integer id) is new logic exercisable without any framework context: it loops visits, guards on isNew(), and uses Objects.equals. Per the pyramid brief, this method should have a unit test. No unit test exists for it. Boundary cases worth covering: visit found, visit not found returns null, visit with isNew()=true is skipped, null id argument.
findings.fix: Add unit tests for Pet.getVisit() in PetTest covering the four boundary cases — no Spring context required.

approved_aspects: All five PRD acceptance criteria have dedicated passing test methods covering prefilled form, redirect on success, in-place count invariant via ArgumentCaptor, blank-description rejection, and past-date rejection.

The in-place update test correctly uses ArgumentCaptor on owners.save(), asserts hasSize(1) on the visits collection, then asserts both the updated date and description — directly exercising the most critical no-add invariant.
The error-code assertion attributeHasFieldErrorCode matching typeMismatch.visitDate for the past-date rejection matches the production validation path precisely.
@WebMvcTest + @MockitoBean reuse is consistent with the file's established style and sanctioned by the design triage and the brief's toleration clause.
Test data in @BeforeEach is deterministic and does not share mutable state across tests.
All eight tests pass with no failures or skips.
